questions.q: What combination actually identifies one specific CloudWatch metric's time series, not just a metric name?
options: The metric name alone, since CloudWatch never reuses metric names across services
The AWS account ID plus the region the metric was published in
The namespace, the metric name, and the full set of dimension values together
The CloudWatch Logs log group that the metric happens to be associated with
questions.explain: A namespace (e.g. AWS/EC2) plus a metric name (e.g. CPUUtilization) plus the full set of dimension values (e.g. InstanceId=i-0a1b2c3d) together uniquely identify one specific metric data stream.

questions.q: What does setting StorageResolution to 1 on a custom metric actually change?
options: It stores a data point as often as every 1 second instead of the 60-second standard-resolution default, at a higher publishing cost
It retains the metric's data for 1 extra year beyond the default retention
It rounds every published value to 1 decimal place before storing it
It limits the metric to exactly 1 dimension so it can be queried faster
questions.explain: High-resolution metrics (StorageResolution as low as 1 second) let alarms evaluate on periods as short as 10 seconds instead of being locked to 60-second boundaries, at the cost of higher PutMetricData volume.

questions.q: In CloudWatch Logs, what is the actual relationship between a log group and a log stream?
options: A log stream is a region-wide container and a log group is one source writing into it
They are two names for the exact same object with no structural difference
A log stream can belong to multiple unrelated log groups at once
A log group is the top-level container (usually one resource or app) and a log stream within it holds events from one single source, like one Lambda execution environment
questions.explain: A log group is scoped to a resource or application (e.g. /aws/lambda/checkout-function) and sets retention; a log stream inside it is a sequence of events from one specific source, such as one Lambda execution environment or one EC2 instance.

questions.q: In a Logs Insights query, what does this line do: `filter @message like /ERROR/`?
options: Narrows the result set to log events whose raw message matches the given pattern
Deletes every log event containing the word ERROR from the log group permanently
Creates a new custom metric named ERROR from matching log lines
Sorts all log events so that ERROR lines appear first, without removing any events
questions.explain: filter narrows the events that continue through the rest of the query pipeline to those matching the condition — it never deletes or modifies the underlying log data, it only filters what the query returns.

questions.q: What does the `parse` command let a Logs Insights query do that `filter` alone cannot?
options: Change the retention period of the log group being queried
Pull structured fields (like a severity level) out of an unstructured raw log message so they can be filtered or aggregated on
Publish the query's results back to CloudWatch as a new custom metric automatically
Query multiple AWS regions' log groups in a single request
questions.explain: parse extracts named fields out of the free-text @message using a pattern (e.g. parse @message "[*] *" as level, msg), so those extracted values can then be used in filter or stats — something a plain substring filter on the raw message can't do.
